title: soft-linger-adapter + fairshare-rescuer: dynamic windowing, timeout hedging and KV-aware starvation prevention
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context and motivation: Our continuous-batching runtime has intermittent request starvation and high tail latency for low-volume, KV-heavy traffic. Earlier work introduced static linger and simple fairness knobs, but real traffic mixes (short, KV-heavy, and long requests) cause harmful oscillation: small requests wait too long for batch fill, while large/slow requests pin slots and starve short ones. This PR introduces two cooperating runtime components: (1) soft-linger-adapter, a dynamic per-queue linger controller that adjusts hold time based on short-request hit-rate and recent kernel execution profile; and (2) fairshare-rescuer, a lightweight admission-time rebalancer that detects KV-cache pinned lanes and hedges timeouts to reschedule/rescue short requests.

Design summary: soft-linger-adapter computes a rolling short-request fraction and effective kernel tail estimate, then gently increases or decreases the linger window (within configured min/max bounds) using an exponential-decay controller so changes are smooth. This reduces batch fill waits for bursty short traffic while still enabling batching for throughput. fairshare-rescuer attaches a small credit budget to each priority cohort; when KV-cache pinning or long-running kernels are detected (via kernel-exec-duration histograms and cache-miss signals), rescuer temporarily raises short-request admission priority and issues a non-blocking hedged probe to an alternate slot/worker to reduce observed starvation. The rescuer is conservative: hedging uses a brief jittered timeout and cancels duplicate work when the primary completes. Both components are KV-aware: hints from the KV cache (pin counts, warmup status) influence rescuer thresholds and linger decay rates.

Compatibility and config: New config knobs (soft_linger.min_ms, soft_linger.max_ms, soft_linger.decay_tau_ms, rescuer.credit_window, rescuer.hedge_timeout_ms, rescuer.kv_pin_threshold) are exposed with reasonable defaults tuned for our production mix. Feature flags allow incremental rollout per-cluster. No API changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: docs/design/batcher_dynamic_linger.md
- [x] Unit tests for adapter and rescuer modules
- [x] Integration tests that reproduce starvation scenarios
- [x] Benchmarks comparing tail p99/p999 before/after
- [x] Telemetry hooks for new metrics

Commits summary: [1/3] introduce soft-linger-adapter core loop, config and metrics; [2/3] add fairshare-rescuer admission-time logic, KV-cache hint plumbing and cancellation plumbing for hedged probes; [3/3] tests, integration harness updates, docs and benchmark results.

Changed areas (high level): src/serving/batcher/soft_linger_adapter.rs - new controller and API; src/serving/scheduler/fairshare_rescuer.rs - admission-time rescuer & hedging; src/serving/kv_cache/prefetch_hint.rs - light-weight pin counters and hint surface; runtime/config/batcher.toml - configs; tests/integration/batcher_starvation_test.py - reproducer; benchmarks/batcher_tail/continuous_bench.py - benchmark harness additions; docs/design/batcher_dynamic_linger.md - design rationale; metrics/observability/metrics_registry.rs - new metrics (batcher.linger_ms, rescuer.hedge_count, rescuer.rescue_rate); examples/ops/continuous_batching_rollout.yaml - rollout procedure.

Testing and results: On the internal benchmark harness that mixes 80% short (<=64 tokens) KV-heavy requests and 20% long-form requests we observe: median latency: +2% (due to slightly increased probe activity), p95: -18%, p99: -32%, p999: -41% for short requests. Starvation incidents (measured as requests waiting > configured timeout without progress) dropped by ~85% in the simulated spike runs. CPU/GPU utilization remained within acceptable bounds; hedging contributes ~1.7% additional request work at peak.

Telemetry and rollout: New metrics were added and wired into the console dashboards (batcher.linger_ms, batcher.short_fraction, rescuer.hedge_count, rescuer.rescue_rate, kv.pin_count). Recommended rollout: enable feature-flag on a non-critical region for 24h, monitor rescue_rate and p99; if rescuer.hedge_count spikes > threshold consider backing off or increasing hedge_timeout.

Backward/forward compatibility: No protocol or API changes; config defaults preserve current behavior. The rescuer and adapter are opt-in via feature flags for gradual adoption.

Followups: (a) kernel-level hints to preemptively migrate KV-warm kernels off hot lanes; (b) tighten autoscaling integration so batcher linger adapts to observed node capacity; (c) distributed coordination experiment for global fairsharing across machines.

review_comments: Ravi: Can we make the hedge timeout adaptive based on observed kernel tail? I asked for a follow-up to experiment with dynamic hedge_timeout_ms
Anika: Left a nit on metric naming and suggested adding a dashboard cell for rescue_rate vs p99 per-model
Jonas: Requested an additional integration test for multi-tenant KV-warm lanes; added test and updated harness
release_notes: Introduce soft-linger-adapter and fairshare-rescuer to reduce starvation and tail latency for mixed KV/short workloads. Opt-in via feature flag. See docs/design/batcher_dynamic_linger.md for rollout guidance.
notes_for_ops: Default config preserves current behavior; enable feature flag in stages. Watch metrics: rescuer.hedge_count, batcher.short_fraction, batcher.linger_ms, and p99 latency. Hedge activity expected but should be small; if rescuer.hedge_count > 1000/min for >10m consider rollback or tuning.
